# The files that can move the mutation score — the single source of truth.
#
# One glob per line, `#` comments and blank lines ignored, matched against paths
# relative to the repository root. Read by two things, which is the whole point:
#
#   * scripts/mutation_relevance.py, which decides at run time whether the
#     expensive steps of .github/workflows/mutation.yml need to happen;
#   * tests/test_mutation_config.py, which recomputes the first-party import
#     closure from the AST and fails if this list is missing anything.
#
# This list used to live in `mutation.yml` as the `paths:` filter on the
# `pull_request` trigger. It moved here so the `mutate` job can run — and
# therefore *report* — on every PR while still doing the work only on the PRs
# that can change the answer. A required check that is skipped never reports:
# GitHub leaves the PR at "Expected — Waiting for status to be reported"
# forever, so requiring it would have deadlocked every docs-only PR. See #19.
#
# Two lists that must agree by hand is the failure mode this file designs out.
# Add a path here — not in the workflow, and not in the test.

# The two mutated modules, from `[tool.mutmut].paths_to_mutate`.
drift/detectors.py
models/backtest.py

# The seven test files named in `[tool.mutmut].runner`, which are the only tests
# that can kill or fail to kill a mutant. Not `tests/**`: most test files here
# cannot move this number, and making an unrelated docs PR wait 36 minutes is
# how a job gets routed around. `tests/test_mutation_config.py` asserts this
# list matches the runner, so the two cannot drift apart.
tests/test_drift_detectors.py
tests/test_drift_boundaries.py
tests/test_drift_timeline.py
tests/test_drift_trigger.py
tests/test_backtest.py
tests/test_backtest_accounting.py
tests/test_baseline.py

# Every first-party module those nine files import, directly or transitively.
# The first version of this filter omitted all of them and was wrong:
# `drift/config.py` holds the `DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS` the boundary tests pin, so
# editing a threshold changes what `drift/detectors.py`'s mutants do while
# touching no listed path. `tests/test_mutation_config.py` recomputes this
# closure from the import graph and fails if anything is missing, so the list
# cannot silently rot.
drift/**
features/**
models/**
ingest/config.py
ingest/store.py

# The lockfile. `uv sync --frozen` installs exactly this, so a pandas, numpy or
# lightgbm bump changes behaviour under a suite nobody touched while matching
# none of the paths above. Dependabot has already opened four PRs here, so most
# dependency change *does* arrive in a commit — and a commit should be caught by
# the trigger that can attribute it rather than left for Monday's cron.
uv.lock

# ...and the tooling that decides the verdict — including the relevance decision
# itself. A change to the matcher changes which PRs get measured, so a change to
# the matcher has to be measured.
pyproject.toml
scripts/mutation_score.py
scripts/mutation_survivors.py
scripts/mutation_relevance.py
.github/mutation-paths.txt
.github/workflows/mutation.yml
